# Lecture 3 — Cell Membranes and Transport

## LO1 — describe the fluid mosaic model of the plasma membrane
**Definition — fluid mosaic model.** the membrane is a dynamic phospholipid bilayer in which proteins float laterally, so structure and function arise from lipid–protein interaction (Singer & Nicolson, 1972).

**Mechanism — why the bilayer self-assembles.** amphipathic phospholipids bury hydrophobic tails away from water, so assembly is entropy-driven rather than requiring energy input.

| component | role | key limitation |
|---|---|---|
| phospholipid | barrier and fluidity | impermeable to ions |
| integral protein | transport and signalling | needs lipid environment |

## LO2a — compare passive and active transport
### passive transport
diffusion and facilitated diffusion move solutes down a gradient with no ATP.

$$J = -D \frac{dC}{dx}$$

- **simple diffusion:** unassisted movement of small non-polar molecules
- **facilitated diffusion:** carrier or channel assisted, still down the gradient

## LO2b — evaluate how the sodium–potassium pump maintains a gradient
> **Exam note — pump stoichiometry.** three Na⁺ out for two K⁺ in per ATP, which makes the pump electrogenic.

The pump counters leak currents and therefore sustains the resting potential.
